activations.domainDescription: Voluntary movement execution and upper motor neuron output
activations.domainFunction: Executes voluntary movement commands via corticospinal tract; Betz cells project to spinal motor neurons
activations.whyThisNode: Primary motor output — M1 is the final cortical station for voluntary movement, directly affected in stroke, ALS, and movement disorders

treatments.label: Constraint-induced movement therapy
treatments.description: Constrains unaffected limb to force use of paretic limb, overcoming learned non-use via neuroplasticity

treatments.label: Motor cortex transcranial magnetic stimulation assessment
treatments.description: TMS motor evoked potentials evaluate corticospinal tract integrity and upper motor neuron function

activations.domainDescription: Motor planning, sequencing, and internally generated movement
activations.domainFunction: Plans and sequences complex voluntary movements; critical for internally-cued motor programs
activations.whyThisNode: Motor planning hub — SMA hypoactivation underlies impaired movement initiation in Parkinson's and motor sequencing deficits in ALS

treatments.label: Rhythmic auditory stimulation for gait
treatments.description: External rhythmic cues bypass defective internal timing to improve gait initiation and cadence

treatments.label: Functional MRI motor mapping
treatments.description: fMRI activation mapping delineates SMA contribution to motor planning deficits pre-surgically

activations.domainDescription: Dopaminergic motor circuit origin and nigrostriatal pathway
activations.domainFunction: Produces dopamine for the nigrostriatal pathway; loss of SNpc neurons is the hallmark of Parkinson's disease
activations.whyThisNode: Dopaminergic motor source — SNpc degeneration is the defining pathology of Parkinson's disease, the second most common neurodegenerative disorder

treatments.label: DaTscan (dopamine transporter imaging)
treatments.description: SPECT imaging of striatal dopamine transporter density to confirm nigrostriatal degeneration

treatments.label: Levodopa/carbidopa initiation
treatments.description: Dopamine precursor replacement therapy for symptomatic Parkinson's disease

activations.domainDescription: Basal ganglia input nucleus for motor and cognitive processing
activations.domainFunction: Integrates cortical input and dopaminergic modulation to select and gate motor programs via direct/indirect pathways
activations.whyThisNode: Movement selection gateway — striatal dopamine depletion drives motor symptoms in Parkinson's; Huntington's disease selectively destroys striatal neurons

treatments.label: Dopamine agonist therapy
treatments.description: Direct D2/D3 receptor stimulation for early Parkinson's to preserve striatal function

treatments.label: MRI volumetric analysis of striatum
treatments.description: Quantitative MRI measures striatal atrophy progression in Huntington's and parkinsonian syndromes

activations.domainDescription: Basal ganglia indirect pathway relay and DBS target
activations.domainFunction: Drives excitatory output to GPi; becomes hyperactive when striatal inhibition fails, suppressing thalamocortical drive
activations.whyThisNode: DBS target for movement disorders — STN hyperactivity is central to parkinsonian bradykinesia, and STN-DBS is the most performed functional neurosurgery worldwide

treatments.label: Deep brain stimulation evaluation
treatments.description: Multidisciplinary assessment for STN-DBS candidacy in medication-refractory Parkinson's disease

treatments.label: Levodopa challenge test
treatments.description: Supratherapeutic levodopa dose assesses motor responsiveness to predict DBS outcomes

activations.domainDescription: Basal ganglia output nucleus controlling thalamocortical drive
activations.domainFunction: GPi provides tonic inhibition of thalamus; excessive GPi output in parkinsonism suppresses movement initiation
activations.whyThisNode: Motor output gatekeeper — GPi over-inhibition of thalamus produces bradykinesia; GPi-DBS is an alternative to STN-DBS for dystonia and Parkinson's

treatments.label: GPi-DBS for dystonia
treatments.description: Pallidal deep brain stimulation is first-line surgical treatment for medication-refractory dystonia

treatments.label: Amantadine for dyskinesia
treatments.description: NMDA antagonist reduces levodopa-induced dyskinesias by modulating pallidal output

activations.domainDescription: Central relay station for motor, sensory, and consciousness circuits
activations.domainFunction: Relays and gates sensory/motor information to cortex; thalamocortical oscillations drive seizures, tremor, and consciousness
activations.whyThisNode: Neural crossroads — thalamic dysfunction underlies seizure propagation, tremor oscillation, pain gating, and consciousness disorders across neurology

treatments.label: VIM thalamotomy (focused ultrasound)
treatments.description: MRI-guided focused ultrasound ablation of VIM thalamus for medication-refractory essential tremor

treatments.label: EEG with thalamocortical rhythm analysis
treatments.description: Scalp EEG evaluates thalamocortical oscillation patterns in seizure disorders and absence epilepsy

activations.domainDescription: Motor coordination, balance, and error correction
activations.domainFunction: Coordinates movement timing, corrects motor errors, and maintains balance via vestibulo-cerebellar and cerebello-thalamo-cortical circuits
activations.whyThisNode: Coordination center — cerebellar dysfunction produces ataxia, intention tremor, and dysmetria in MS, stroke, and hereditary ataxias

treatments.label: Balance and coordination rehabilitation
treatments.description: Vestibular and proprioceptive retraining exercises for cerebellar ataxia management

treatments.label: MRI posterior fossa evaluation
treatments.description: High-resolution MRI assesses cerebellar lesions, atrophy, and posterior fossa structural abnormalities

activations.domainDescription: Episodic memory formation and temporal lobe epilepsy focus
activations.domainFunction: Encodes new episodic memories; hippocampal sclerosis is the most common pathology in temporal lobe epilepsy
activations.whyThisNode: Memory and seizure nexus — hippocampal atrophy is the earliest structural marker of Alzheimer's, and hippocampal sclerosis drives temporal lobe epilepsy

treatments.label: Hippocampal volumetry on MRI
treatments.description: Quantitative hippocampal volume measurement tracks Alzheimer's progression and epilepsy lateralization

treatments.label: Cholinesterase inhibitor therapy
treatments.description: Donepezil/rivastigmine increases hippocampal cholinergic transmission in Alzheimer's disease

activations.domainDescription: GABAergic inhibition and glutamatergic excitation equilibrium
activations.domainFunction: Maintains cortical excitation-inhibition balance; failure triggers seizures, excitotoxicity, and neurodegeneration
activations.whyThisNode: Seizure threshold controller — GABA/glutamate imbalance is the fundamental mechanism of epilepsy and contributes to excitotoxic neuronal death across disorders

treatments.label: Antiepileptic drug selection
treatments.description: Targeted AED therapy based on seizure type: sodium channel blockers, GABA enhancers, or SV2A modulators

treatments.label: Therapeutic drug level monitoring
treatments.description: Serum AED levels ensure therapeutic range and guide dose adjustments to prevent breakthrough seizures

activations.domainDescription: Central pain modulation and migraine generator
activations.domainFunction: Orchestrates descending pain modulation; dysfunction as migraine generator allows trigeminovascular activation
activations.whyThisNode: Pain control center — PAG dysfunction is implicated in migraine chronification, and PAG lesions cause central pain syndromes

treatments.label: CGRP monoclonal antibody therapy
treatments.description: Anti-CGRP antibodies (erenumab, fremanezumab) for migraine prevention targeting trigeminovascular pathway

treatments.label: Headache diary and trigger identification
treatments.description: Systematic tracking of headache frequency, triggers, and medication use to guide treatment decisions

activations.domainDescription: Expressive language production and motor speech
activations.domainFunction: Produces fluent speech output; damage causes non-fluent aphasia with preserved comprehension
activations.whyThisNode: Speech production center — Broca's area infarction in left MCA stroke causes expressive aphasia, one of the most devastating stroke outcomes

treatments.label: Aphasia rehabilitation (speech-language therapy)
treatments.description: Intensive constraint-induced language therapy and melodic intonation therapy for post-stroke aphasia

treatments.label: Acute stroke language assessment (NIHSS)
treatments.description: Bedside language testing within NIHSS quantifies aphasia severity and guides thrombolysis/thrombectomy decisions

activations.domainDescription: Language comprehension and auditory processing
activations.domainFunction: Decodes spoken and written language; damage causes fluent aphasia with impaired comprehension
activations.whyThisNode: Comprehension center — Wernicke's area damage in posterior temporal stroke produces receptive aphasia, and language network disruption occurs in Alzheimer's and FTD

treatments.label: Comprehensive aphasia assessment
treatments.description: Western Aphasia Battery and Boston Diagnostic Aphasia Exam classify aphasia type and guide therapy

treatments.label: Augmentative communication devices
treatments.description: Speech-generating devices and communication boards for severe comprehension or expression deficits

activations.domainDescription: Visual processing, aura generation, and optic pathway
activations.domainFunction: Processes visual input from retina via LGN; cortical spreading depression in V1 generates migraine aura
activations.whyThisNode: Visual processing and aura origin — V1 hyperexcitability drives migraine with aura, PCA stroke causes hemianopia, and optic neuritis is the hallmark of MS

treatments.label: Visual field perimetry
treatments.description: Automated perimetry maps visual field defects from optic neuritis, stroke, or compressive lesions

treatments.label: Neuromodulation for migraine with aura
treatments.description: Single-pulse TMS (sTMS) device applied to occipital cortex aborts cortical spreading depression during aura

activations.domainDescription: Somatic sensation processing and central sensitization
activations.domainFunction: Processes touch, pain, and proprioceptive input; central sensitization in S1 drives allodynia in migraine and neuropathic pain
activations.whyThisNode: Sensory gateway — S1 hyperexcitability produces cutaneous allodynia in chronic migraine, and somatosensory stroke causes contralateral numbness

treatments.label: Quantitative sensory testing
treatments.description: Standardized testing of thermal, vibration, and pain thresholds maps somatosensory dysfunction

treatments.label: Botulinum toxin for chronic migraine
treatments.description: OnabotulinumtoxinA 31-site injection protocol reduces peripheral trigeminal sensitization and central S1 hyperexcitability

crossDomainAffinities.role: Anticipatory Anxiety Generator — Signal Detection & Input — Secondary Node

activations.domainDescription: Interhemispheric white matter connectivity
activations.domainFunction: Connects homologous cortical regions across hemispheres; demyelination disrupts bilateral coordination and cognitive integration
activations.whyThisNode: Interhemispheric bridge — corpus callosum Dawson finger lesions are pathognomonic for MS, and callosal disconnection affects stroke recovery and ALS-FTD

treatments.label: MRI with DTI tractography
treatments.description: Diffusion tensor imaging maps white matter tract integrity and demyelination burden in MS and ALS

treatments.label: Disease-modifying therapy for MS
treatments.description: High-efficacy DMTs (anti-CD20, natalizumab) reduce new lesion formation and slow white matter damage

activations.domainDescription: CNS innate immune activation and inflammatory cascades
activations.domainFunction: Resident brain immune cells activate in response to injury and disease; chronic activation drives neurodegeneration across disorders
activations.whyThisNode: Neuroinflammation driver — microglial activation is central to MS, Alzheimer's amyloid response, post-stroke injury, and neurodegenerative disease progression

treatments.label: Anti-CD20 B-cell depletion therapy
treatments.description: Ocrelizumab/ofatumumab targets B-cell-driven neuroinflammation in relapsing and progressive MS

treatments.label: CSF inflammatory marker panel
treatments.description: CSF oligoclonal bands, IgG index, and cell count differentiate inflammatory from non-inflammatory CNS conditions

activations.domainDescription: Executive function, working memory, and cognitive control
activations.domainFunction: Coordinates executive function, working memory, and cognitive flexibility; disrupted in MS cognitive impairment and ALS-FTD spectrum
activations.whyThisNode: Executive control center — dlPFC dysfunction underlies cognitive impairment in MS (most common deficit), ALS-FTD spectrum, and post-stroke executive dysfunction

treatments.label: Neuropsychological testing battery
treatments.description: Standardized cognitive assessment (BICAMS for MS, ECAS for ALS) quantifies executive and processing speed deficits

treatments.label: Cognitive rehabilitation program
treatments.description: Computer-based and strategy-based cognitive training targeting processing speed and working memory deficits

activations.domainDescription: Cortical rhythms, pathological oscillations, and synchrony
activations.domainFunction: Normal oscillatory activity coordinates neural communication; pathological oscillations drive seizures, tremor, and absence epilepsy
activations.whyThisNode: Rhythm and synchrony — pathological high-frequency oscillations mark seizure onset zones, 3 Hz spike-wave drives absence epilepsy, and beta oscillations are disrupted in Parkinson's

treatments.label: Prolonged video-EEG monitoring
treatments.description: Continuous EEG captures ictal events, localizes seizure onset, and identifies pathological oscillation patterns

treatments.label: Responsive neurostimulation (RNS)
treatments.description: Closed-loop intracranial stimulation detects and disrupts pathological oscillations at seizure onset in real time

activations.domainDescription: Noradrenergic arousal, migraine premonitory phase, and autonomic regulation
activations.domainFunction: Primary brain norepinephrine source; modulates arousal, attention, and autonomic function; degeneration contributes to PD non-motor symptoms
activations.whyThisNode: Noradrenergic modulator — LC activation drives migraine premonitory symptoms, LC degeneration causes PD depression and RBD, and LC norepinephrine modulates seizure threshold

treatments.label: Beta-blocker migraine prophylaxis
treatments.description: Propranolol modulates noradrenergic tone and reduces migraine attack frequency

treatments.label: Sleep behavior assessment
treatments.description: REM sleep behavior disorder screening as prodromal marker of synucleinopathy (PD, Lewy body dementia)

activations.domainDescription: Serotonergic pain modulation and migraine pathophysiology
activations.domainFunction: Primary brain serotonin source; modulates pain descending pathways; serotonergic dysfunction is central to migraine pathophysiology
activations.whyThisNode: Serotonin and pain hub — dorsal raphe dysfunction underlies migraine (triptans act on 5-HT1B/1D receptors), and serotonergic degeneration contributes to PD depression

treatments.label: Triptan therapy for acute migraine
treatments.description: Sumatriptan/rizatriptan activates 5-HT1B/1D receptors to abort migraine by inhibiting trigeminovascular CGRP release

treatments.label: Medication overuse headache screening
treatments.description: Assess triptan and analgesic use frequency; >10 days/month indicates medication overuse headache risk

activations.domainDescription: Neuroplasticity, neuroprotection, and recovery signaling
activations.domainFunction: Supports neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis; critical for post-injury recovery and rehabilitation outcomes
activations.whyThisNode: Neuroplasticity signal — BDNF genotype predicts stroke rehabilitation outcomes, exercise-induced BDNF supports Alzheimer's neuroprotection, and BDNF signaling is disrupted in neurodegeneration

treatments.label: Aerobic exercise prescription (150 min/week)
treatments.description: Regular aerobic exercise upregulates BDNF, preserves hippocampal volume, and improves outcomes across neurological conditions

treatments.label: BDNF Val66Met genotyping (research)
treatments.description: BDNF polymorphism testing may predict rehabilitation responsiveness in stroke and neurodegenerative conditions

activations.domainDescription: Consciousness, arousal, and respiratory drive
activations.domainFunction: Maintains consciousness and arousal via ascending reticular activating system; drives respiratory rhythm generation
activations.whyThisNode: Consciousness and breathing — RF dysfunction causes loss of consciousness in generalized seizures, pontine hemorrhage causes coma, and RF degeneration in ALS causes respiratory failure

treatments.label: Pulmonary function monitoring (FVC)
treatments.description: Serial forced vital capacity testing detects respiratory muscle decline in ALS and neuromuscular diseases

treatments.label: Non-invasive ventilation (BiPAP)
treatments.description: Bilevel positive airway pressure extends survival and improves quality of life in ALS respiratory decline

activations.domainDescription: Speech production, swallowing, and airway protection
activations.domainFunction: Controls vocal cord movement, swallowing coordination, and airway protection; bulbar motor neuron loss causes dysarthria and dysphagia
activations.whyThisNode: Bulbar function center — laryngeal motor neuron loss causes progressive dysarthria and dysphagia in ALS, and bulbar dysfunction creates aspiration risk in stroke and myasthenia

treatments.label: Videofluoroscopic swallow study
treatments.description: Dynamic imaging of swallowing mechanics identifies aspiration risk and guides diet modification in bulbar dysfunction

treatments.label: LSVT LOUD speech therapy
treatments.description: Amplitude-focused intensive speech therapy for Parkinson's hypophonia and ALS dysarthria

activations.domainDescription: Autonomic regulation, migraine premonitory phase, and sleep-wake cycling
activations.domainFunction: Regulates autonomic homeostasis, circadian rhythms, and neuroendocrine function; hypothalamic activation initiates migraine premonitory phase
activations.whyThisNode: Autonomic command center — hypothalamic activation drives migraine prodrome (yawning, cravings), cluster headache circadian pattern, and sleep disorder pathophysiology

treatments.label: Sleep-wake cycle evaluation
treatments.description: Actigraphy and polysomnography assess circadian disruption contributing to headache and seizure disorders

treatments.label: Circadian rhythm stabilization
treatments.description: Regular sleep-wake schedule, light therapy, and melatonin to stabilize hypothalamic circadian output

issues.label: Parkinson's Disease
issues.summary: Progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta disrupts basal ganglia motor circuit, causing bradykinesia, rigidity, and tremor

circuits.detail: substantia nigra — dopamine / motor gating — parkinsonian rigidity

_authored.detail: Dopaminergic neuronal loss in SNpc — hallmark pathology; >60% loss before symptom onset
Striatal dopamine depletion (putamen > caudate) — motor symptoms correlate with putaminal loss
Subthalamic nucleus overactive due to reduced GPe inhibition — primary DBS target
GPi output excessive — over-inhibits thalamus, suppressing motor cortex activation
Thalamocortical drive suppressed by GPi over-inhibition producing bradykinesia
Motor cortex hypoactivation — reduced movement initiation and amplitude
Supplementary motor area underactivated — impaired internally-generated movement sequencing
Mesolimbic dopamine loss causing apathy, anhedonia, and depression in PD
Pedunculopontine nucleus degeneration causing postural instability and gait freezing
Olfactory bulb alpha-synuclein deposition — hyposmia is earliest premotor symptom
Noradrenergic cell loss contributing to depression, REM sleep behavior disorder, and orthostatic hypotension

issues.label: Alzheimer's Disease
issues.summary: Amyloid-beta plaques and neurofibrillary tau tangles cause progressive neuronal loss beginning in entorhinal cortex and hippocampus, spreading to association cortices

circuits.detail: entorhinal — hippocampal memory gateway — encoding failure

_authored.detail: Hippocampal atrophy — earliest structural change; correlates with episodic memory loss
Entorhinal cortex first region affected by tau pathology; gateway to hippocampal memory circuit
Nucleus basalis of Meynert cholinergic neuron loss — basis for cholinesterase inhibitor therapy
Posterior cingulate/precuneus hypometabolism — earliest FDG-PET finding; DMN hub disrupted
Default mode network progressively disconnects — amyloid deposition follows DMN topology
Precuneus hypometabolism and atrophy — correlates with episodic memory and self-referential processing loss
Angular gyrus atrophy — contributes to semantic memory loss and spatial disorientation
Language network degradation — word-finding difficulty progressing to aphasia in later stages
Microglial neuroinflammation — activated microglia surround plaques; inflammatory cascade amplifies neuronal damage

issues.label: Migraine
issues.summary: Cortical spreading depression triggers trigeminovascular activation; CGRP release from trigeminal afferents causes neurogenic inflammation and thalamic sensitization drives photophobia and allodynia

_authored.detail: Thalamic sensitization amplifies sensory signals producing photophobia, phonophobia, and allodynia
PAG dysfunction as migraine generator — iron deposits found in chronic migraineurs; descending pain modulation fails
Locus coeruleus activation during premonitory phase — photophobia and arousal changes
Dorsal raphe serotonergic dysfunction — triptans act via 5-HT1B/1D receptors on trigeminal nerves
Somatosensory cortex hyperexcitable during migraine — cutaneous allodynia via central sensitization
Visual cortex hyperexcitability — cortical spreading depression originates in occipital cortex during aura
Hypothalamic activation in premonitory phase — yawning, food cravings, mood changes before headache
Insula processes pain and interoceptive signals — activated during migraine attacks

issues.label: Multiple Sclerosis
issues.summary: Autoimmune demyelination in CNS white matter with axonal damage creating multifocal lesions disseminated in space and time, preferentially affecting optic nerve, periventricular white matter, and spinal cord

_authored.detail: Corpus callosum lesions (Dawson fingers) disrupt interhemispheric connectivity — hallmark MS location
Optic nerve demyelination (optic neuritis) — most common presenting symptom; afferent pupillary defect
Cerebellar and brainstem lesions producing ataxia, intention tremor, nystagmus, and scanning speech
Corticospinal tract demyelination producing upper motor neuron signs: spasticity, weakness, hyperreflexia
Hippocampal atrophy contributes to memory impairment present in 40-65% of MS patients
Frontal white matter lesions disrupt processing speed and executive function — most common cognitive deficit
Activated microglia drive chronic neuroinflammation — targets of emerging MS therapies
Widespread white matter disconnection disrupts distributed cognitive networks

issues.label: Ischemic Stroke
issues.summary: Acute interruption of cerebral blood flow by thrombus or embolism causes core infarct and salvageable penumbra; time-dependent neural circuit damage depends on vascular territory

circuits.detail: primary motor cortex — motor output — weakness, paresis

_authored.detail: MCA territory motor cortex infarction producing contralateral hemiparesis (most common deficit)
Left MCA inferior frontal infarction producing expressive (Broca) aphasia
Left posterior temporal infarction producing receptive (Wernicke) aphasia
Strategic thalamic infarct can cause memory loss, apathy, or aphasia depending on nuclei affected
PCA territory infarction producing contralateral homonymous hemianopia
Cerebellar stroke causing ataxia, vertigo, dysmetria; risk of posterior fossa edema and herniation
White matter tract damage disrupts interhemispheric transfer and distributed network function
BDNF Val66Met polymorphism affects post-stroke neuroplasticity and rehabilitation outcomes

issues.label: Focal (Partial) Seizures
issues.summary: Abnormal hypersynchronous discharge originating in a localized cortical focus; thalamocortical loops amplify and propagate ictal activity while GABAergic inhibition fails locally

_authored.detail: Thalamocortical relay neurons entrained into hypersynchronous oscillations during seizure propagation
Hippocampal sclerosis and mossy fiber sprouting create recurrent excitatory loops
GABAergic interneuron failure with unopposed glutamatergic excitation at seizure focus
Insular cortex involvement in autonomic seizure semiology (ictal tachycardia, epigastric aura)
Amygdala kindling model — repeated subthreshold stimulation lowers seizure threshold
Motor cortex involvement produces contralateral clonic movements in motor-onset seizures
Pathological high-frequency oscillations (250-500 Hz ripples) mark seizure onset zone
Cerebellar modulation of cortical excitability disrupted; potential seizure suppression role

issues.label: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
issues.summary: Progressive degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons with TDP-43 proteinopathy; motor cortex UMN loss causes spasticity and anterior horn LMN loss causes weakness, atrophy, and fasciculations

circuits.detail: primary motor cortex — motor output — weakness, paresis

_authored.detail: Betz cell (upper motor neuron) degeneration in primary motor cortex producing spasticity and hyperreflexia
Premotor cortex involvement producing impaired motor planning and sequencing
Bulbar onset: corticobulbar degeneration producing dysarthria, dysphagia, and pseudobulbar affect
Frontotemporal dysfunction in 50% — executive and behavioral changes even without full FTD
Laryngeal motor neuron loss producing voice weakness and eventual inability to speak
Phrenic motor neuron and brainstem respiratory center degeneration producing respiratory failure
Corticospinal tract degeneration visible on DTI; corpus callosum involvement in ALS-FTD

issues.label: Essential Tremor
issues.summary: Cerebello-thalamo-cortical circuit oscillation at 4-12 Hz driven by Purkinje cell loss in cerebellar cortex, with VIM thalamic relay of pathological oscillation to motor cortex

_authored.detail: Purkinje cell loss in cerebellar cortex; cerebellar output dysregulated
VIM thalamic nucleus relays cerebellar oscillation to motor cortex — primary DBS/lesion target
Motor cortex receives oscillatory input from VIM producing rhythmic tremor output
GABAergic deficit suggested by ethanol responsiveness and reduced GABA in cerebellar dentate
Coherent oscillatory activity at tremor frequency in cerebello-thalamo-cortical loop
Neocerebellum (lateral hemispheres) shows metabolic hyperactivity during tremor
